title: EarLog: Opportunistic Ear Physiology Sensing toward Personalized Hearing Risk Awareness
abstract: arXiv:2610.12501v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Many headphone users risk irreversible hearing damage during high-load listening, yet current protection still relies on sound-pressure limits. Clinical tests detect damage after it becomes measurable, leaving the risk-accumulating process unobserved. The acoustic reflex (AR), an involuntary response to high acoustic load, marks when the ear enters a protective state. AR traces are weak, and existing measurements require dedicated probes and controlled conditions that are difficult to maintain during everyday audio. We present EarLog, which turns playback, the dominant interference, into an opportunistic probe. EarLog introduces content-conditioned residual sensing to suppress variations caused by nonstationary content, individual ear acoustics, and device response. It identifies weak AR through loudness-dependent changes and localized spectral irregularities in the residual. A resonance-constrained sparse finite impulse response (FIR)

translated_title: EarLog：面向个性化听力风险感知的机会式耳部生理感知
translated_abstract: 许多耳机用户在高负荷聆听过程中面临不可逆听力损伤的风险，然而目前的保护手段仍依赖于声压限制。临床检测只能在损伤已经可测量之后才发现问题，使得风险累积的过程处于未被观测的状态。声反射（Acoustic Reflex, AR）是一种对高声学负荷的非自主生理反应，标志着耳朵进入保护状态的时机。然而AR信号十分微弱，现有的测量方法需要专用探头和受控条件，而这些条件在日常音频播放中难以维持。我们提出了EarLog，它将播放内容——最主要的干扰源——转变为机会式的探测信号。EarLog引入了内容条件化的残差感知方法，以抑制由非平稳音频内容、个体耳部声学特性差异和设备响应所引起的变异。该方法通过响度相关的变化以及残差中的局部频谱不规则性来识别微弱的AR信号。一种共振约束的稀疏有限冲激响应（FIR）滤波器……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: EarLog将耳机播放内容本身转化为机会式探测信号，通过内容条件化残差感知在日常聆听中识别微弱的声反射，实现对个性化听力损伤风险的实时感知。
en_tdlr: EarLog turns audio playback itself into an opportunistic probe, using content-conditioned residual sensing to detect weak acoustic reflexes during everyday listening and enable personalized hearing risk awareness.
